problem: State-of-the-art ObjectNav methods are either end-to-end RL/IL or modular pipelines with an RL-trained exploration policy (SemExp needs 10M frames). These are costly to train, hard to debug and poorly explainable. Standard ObjectNav evaluation also assumes ground-truth GPS+compass localization, which hides the sim-to-real effect of odometry error.
motivation: ObjectNav can be split into two parts: inferring where the target is likely to be (semantic reasoning) and point-to-point planning (geometry). Classic V-SLAM plus frontier exploration already covers the geometric part without any training. The authors argue that commonsense object-object spatial priors, taken from language models or scene statistics and injected into frontiers, can replace a learned exploration policy. A modular pipeline also lets them swap in ground truth per module to locate the real bottleneck.
key_idea: Build a structured scene representation with classic RTAB-Map SLAM (semantic point cloud, 2D occupancy map, spatial scene graph), then score geometric frontiers with a semantic utility. The utility propagates prior category-to-category distances (from BERT embeddings or Gibson statistics) from nearby observed objects to each frontier, so no navigation policy is trained.
insight: Pure geometric frontier exploration (GeoUtil) is already strong on Gibson (62.3 SR / 35.9 SPL, vs SemExp 65.0 / 33.0). Adding BERT-based semantic frontier scores mostly improves efficiency (SPL 35.9→40.5) and success (62.3→69.3). How semantics are propagated matters: replacing the soft-radius weighting with a hard radius collapses performance back to GeoUtil level (62.4 SR). BERT priors beat CLIP priors (67.7 SR), suggesting that visual-textual similarity is not the same as indoor spatial proximity. The pipeline ablation shows semantic segmentation is the main bottleneck: GT segmentation lifts SR 69.3→84.2, while GT scene graph adds almost nothing (84.9). Replacing GT pose with RTAB-Map odometry drops SR 69.3→57.6. Label confusion hurts far more than missed detections: P(replace)=0.5 gives 35.1 SR, whereas P(drop)=0.5 gives 84.7 SR because multi-frame 3D fusion recovers dropped labels.
method: Semantic V-SLAM: RTAB-Map estimates pose (or uses GT odometry, running only map assembler/optimizer) and builds a dense RGB point cloud. A second RTAB-Map instance fuses Mask R-CNN (Detectron2 pre-trained) semantic masks into a 3D semantic point cloud by back-projection.
2D occupancy map: the 3D reconstruction is projected to the xy-plane; frontiers are cluster centers of explored/unexplored boundary pixels (Yamauchi), each with a position and a length.

Spatial scene graph: DBSCAN (eps 1.0, min 5 points) clusters the semantic point cloud, using the semantic label scaled by a large factor as a 4th dimension. 3D NMS (IoU 0.4) removes spurious small clusters. Nodes are object centers + labels; edges are 3D translations.
Geometric utility: u_geo = frontier length / geodesic distance on the occupancy map (greedy frontier exploration).

Semantic utility (SemFrontier): u_sem = (r·w) / (k·dist). Relation score r_jc = 1/d_jc comes from a prior category-distance matrix (BERT or CLIP word-embedding distance, or Gibson train-scene statistics). Weight w_jc = 1/sqrt(v_jc) comes from a Gibson distance-variance matrix. Objects are aggregated with a soft radius, i.e. inverse object-to-frontier distance as an extra weight.

Policy: follow the geometric utility for the first 50 steps, then purely the semantic utility. Once the target is detected in the current frame, navigate to it; a global planner plus local planner outputs discrete actions and STOP when the goal is reached.

setting.backbone: Training-free modular pipeline: RTAB-Map SLAM + Mask R-CNN (Detectron2 pre-trained, frozen) for segmentation + BERT word-embedding category priors + hand-designed frontier utility
setting.training_data: none (training-free); uses off-the-shelf pre-trained Mask R-CNN and BERT/CLIP text embeddings; a category-distance variance matrix (and the Gibson-prior variant's distance matrix) is computed from GT object layouts of the 25 Gibson train scenes
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, 79° FOV, 5 m max depth) + GT GPS/compass pose in main setting (or RTAB-Map visual odometry in realistic setting)
setting.privileged: main results use GT pose (standard GPS+compass setting); pipeline ablations additionally use GT semantic segmentation (3DSceneGraph) and GT scene graph (masked to explored area)

results: On Gibson ObjectNav (SemExp 1000-episode val set, GT pose), training-free StructNav with BERT priors reaches 69.3 SR / 40.5 SPL / 1.488 DTG. This beats SemExp (65.0 / 33.0 / 1.576), which is trained with RL, and RegQLearn (63.7 / 31.3 / 1.568); the authors report relative gains of 6.6% SR and 22.7% SPL. With RTAB-Map odometry instead of GT pose, performance drops to 57.6 SR, and with GT segmentation it rises to 84.2 SR, identifying perception as the bottleneck.
limitations: Evaluated only on the small Gibson ObjectNav setup (5 val scenes, SemExp episodes) in simulation; no HM3D/MP3D results and no real-robot experiment despite claimed ROS deployability.

Relies heavily on the pre-trained Mask R-CNN (the main bottleneck), and uses hand-tuned heuristics: a fixed 50-step geometric-then-semantic switch and DBSCAN/NMS thresholds. The 'training-free' priors still use Gibson train-scene statistics for the variance weighting.

The headline SOTA claim assumes GT pose. With realistic visual odometry, SR (57.6) falls below the RL baselines, and the simulator's sliding makes localization errors less harmful than on a real robot.
